skill.name: webapp-sqlmap
skill.description: Guides authorized SQLMap testing for SQL injection detection, database enumeration, controlled impact validation, and reporting.
skill.summary: Use SQLMap to assess SQL injection risk in authorized web application tests.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most template and reference-file detections are false positives because they are documentation, detection-rule examples, or CI reporting helpers. Confirmed risk remains high due to SQLMap guidance for data extraction, WAF evasion, file access, shell access, and a CI curl-to-shell installer.

remediation.issue: Advanced SQLMap examples enable file access, web shell upload, and shell access.
remediation.suggestion: Remove these examples or gate them behind explicit authorization, lab-only targets, and safer impact-validation alternatives.

remediation.issue: The CI template installs tfsec with curl piped directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Use a pinned release, package manager, checksum verification, or a trusted action instead of executing a remote script.

remediation.issue: WAF evasion guidance can support unauthorized stealth testing.
remediation.suggestion: Limit evasion content to approved lab use and require written approval before tamper scripts, Tor, proxies, or randomization.

remediation.issue: Data extraction examples include password and full-database dumping.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer minimal proof-of-impact steps, redaction, stopping criteria, and data retention instructions.

remediation.issue: SQLMap output paths can retain sensitive target data.
remediation.suggestion: Add cleanup, encryption, access control, and retention guidance for ~/.sqlmap/output and SQLite session files.

content.value_statement: SQL injection testing can miss vulnerable parameters or produce weak evidence. This skill guides authorized SQLMap workflows for detection, enumeration, controlled extraction, and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Guides SQLMap testing for GET, POST, cookie, header, and request-file inputs.
Explains detection levels, injection techniques, DBMS fingerprinting, and parameter selection.
Provides database enumeration and controlled extraction workflows for authorized assessments.
Covers Burp Suite proxy use, output handling, session resume, and logging.
Includes defensive remediation guidance for preventing SQL injection.
Supplies CI and rule templates for related security checks.
limitations: Requires written authorization and a valid SQLMap installation.
Commands are examples and must be scoped to approved targets.
Does not verify findings automatically or replace manual validation.
Includes high-risk exploitation examples that require strict controls.

use_cases.title: Validate Injection Findings
use_cases.description: Plan SQLMap checks that confirm vulnerable parameters and collect evidence without exceeding the assessment scope.

use_cases.title: Review Application Exposure
use_cases.description: Map database enumeration risk and prepare remediation guidance for vulnerable endpoints.

use_cases.title: Standardize Assessment Workflow
use_cases.description: Create repeatable SQL injection testing steps, reporting notes, and cleanup requirements for a security team.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Authorized Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scoped SQLMap test plan for this endpoint. Include authorization checks, safe options, evidence goals, and cleanup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Detection Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend SQLMap detection settings for these request details. Explain risk level, parameter choice, and manual validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Enumeration Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether database enumeration is justified for this engagement. Define allowed data, stopping points, and reporting boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Build Evidence Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a controlled impact-validation plan for a confirmed SQL injection. Minimize data access and include redaction and stakeholder approvals.

output_examples.input: A tester needs to check a login form during an approved assessment.
output_examples.output: A scoped test plan with authorization checks, selected parameters, safe detection settings, and evidence notes.

output_examples.input: An AppSec engineer found a possible SQL injection in a search endpoint.
output_examples.output: A validation checklist covering parameter selection, DBMS fingerprinting, manual confirmation, and remediation advice.

output_examples.input: A security lead wants a report summary after controlled SQLMap testing.
output_examples.output: A concise findings summary with affected endpoints, verified impact, data handling notes, and recommended fixes.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, testing windows, and data handling rules before running SQLMap.
Use the least invasive options that can prove impact and stop when evidence is sufficient.
Redact sensitive data from reports and remove SQLMap output after retention requirements are met.
anti_patterns: Running examples against systems without explicit permission.
Dumping full databases when limited evidence would satisfy the engagement goal.
Using evasion, shells, or file-write features without written approval.

faq.question: Is this skill only for authorized testing?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it only on systems you own or have written permission to test.

faq.question: Does it install SQLMap?
faq.answer: No. It assumes SQLMap and required dependencies are already available.

faq.question: Can it replace manual validation?
faq.answer: No. SQLMap output should be reviewed and confirmed before reporting a vulnerability.

faq.question: Does it include high-risk examples?
faq.answer: Yes. Some examples cover extraction, evasion, file access, and shell access.

faq.question: How should extracted data be handled?
faq.answer: Access the minimum data needed, redact reports, and follow the engagement data rules.

faq.question: What defensive guidance is included?
faq.answer: It recommends parameterized queries, input validation, least-privilege database accounts, monitoring, and WAF controls.
